title: Coordinating LED Night Illumination in our National Infrastructure
what_it_is: Coordinating LED Night Illumination in our National Infrastructure

sections.label: Warmer LED night lighting
sections.summary: The speaker calls on MND and HDB to standardise LEDs with less blue light and study perceived brightness for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And even if we leave aside the discussion about health implications, there is something to be said for having the night-time lighting look just that little bit more natural − a more yellow shade of white, a city at night that looks warmer and more natural.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, Mr Deputy Speaker, I call upon the Ministry of National Development (MND) and HDB to look at this issue to consider standardising and moving towards LEDs which give out less blue light.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We can do this by choosing LED lights with a bit more of a natural yellow colour, or a "warm white" colour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To ensure that our living environment is still bright enough for the elderly, HDB could also study the perceived brightness of different types of LEDs.

sections.label: LED replacement in streetlamps and schools
sections.summary: With LTA replacing all streetlamps with LEDs by 2022, the speaker says warm yellow-white LEDs could be considered for MOE schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: With LTA's plans to replace all streetlamps with LED lights by 2022, we are at an inflection point in our national lighting infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is not too early for us to be thinking about these questions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And in our Ministry of Education (MOE) schools as well, there may be a role for looking at warm yellow-white LEDs when replacing the older fluorescent light tubes.

sections.label: Colour of night and health
sections.summary: The passage states that the colour of night matters and emerging evidence links better colouring of night to reduced sleep and health risk.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The colour of night matters, and there is emerging evidence that by choosing a better way to colour the night, we can reduce the risk of casting a shadow on our sleep and our health.

sections.label: HDB and LTA lighting studies
sections.summary: HDB will study varying lighting by LED colour; LTA keeps pure white on expressways and major roads and will study warm white for minor roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: HDB will also take up Dr Tan's suggestion to study how to vary lighting levels or luminescence based on different colours of LED lights.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: On its part, LTA will continue to use pure white lighting for expressways and major arterial roads for road safety reasons, because of the greater colour contrast.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In the meantime, because streetlamps use high intensity lighting, LTA will study whether it is feasible to use warm white lighting for streetlamps on minor roads, especially those located in residential estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, the scientific research into lighting is evolving and new lighting solutions will come on the market.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will continue to take steps to find better ways to colour the night, to keep our city vibrant and safe.
